protocol.instrument_name: Authority – Supply of specified restricted substances by pharmacists – management of allergic and non-allergic rhinitis
protocol.instrument_version: Dated: 25 February 2026 (Dr Kerry Chant, Chief Health Officer; Delegation Number PH380, PH381, PH427). Revokes the instrument of Authority – Supply of restricted substances by pharmacists relating to the management of allergic and nonallergic rhinitis dated 30 January 2025.
protocol.effective_date: 2026-02-25 (instrument dated 25 February 2026; 'This authority commences on publication.' — publication date not printed; 'This authority is cancelled on 1 March 2027, unless earlier cancelled.')
protocol.legal_basis: Section 10(4)(d) of the Poisons and Therapeutic Goods Act 1966 and clauses 170, and 171 for the purpose of clause 53 of the Poisons and Therapeutic Goods Regulation 2008. Issued by Dr Kerry Chant, Chief Health Officer, a duly appointed delegate of the Secretary, NSW Health.
protocol.supervision_model: Document's own terminology: an 'approved pharmacist' (holding general registration under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law (NSW), employed or engaged in an 'approved pharmacy', having successfully completed the specified training options, and having provided NSW Health with their details via the expanded-services form) may supply to an applicable patient a restricted substance listed in clause 2 'otherwise than on prescription subject to the conditions in clause 3 of this instrument'.
protocol.scope_summary: NSW Health Authority instrument (legal authorisation, not a clinical practice standard) permitting an approved pharmacist to supply intranasal Fluticasone furoate or Olopatadine with mometasone, and eye drop Olopatadine 0.1%, otherwise than on prescription for the management of allergic and non-allergic rhinitis in an applicable patient (6 years of age or over), subject to the conditions in clause 3 including an absolute 12-week supply cap. Clinical limits (duration of management, quantity, age or other factor limitations and circumstances requiring referral) are set by the separate 'NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Allergic and Nonallergic Rhinitis', which is not part of this document.

inclusion.text: The patient is an 'applicable patient' — 'An 'applicable patient' means a patient 6 years of age or over.'
'The pharmacist must only supply a medicine indicate in clause 2 for the management of allergic and/or nonallergic rhinitis.' [printed as 'indicate']
The medicine supplied is one of the restricted substances listed in clause 2 — 'Intranasal forms of: Fluticasone furoate; Olopatadine with mometasone AND Eye drop forms of: Olopatadine 0.1%'.

provenance.section_heading: 2) Restricted substance to which this instrument applies

inclusion.text: Supply quantity does not exceed the duration of management specified in the Practice Standard, except in the circumstances described in clause 3(c) (smallest available manufacturer's pack).

'Despite clause 3(c), the pharmacist must not supply a medicine indicated in clause 2 of this instrument in a quantity which would result in supply for a period that is longer than 12 weeks.' (supply must not exceed 12 weeks)

'The pharmacist acts in accordance with the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Allergic and Nonallergic Rhinitis approved by the Chief Health Officer and published on the NSW Health website, including in relation to any limitations on the supply of medicines indicated in clause 2, to a patient based on their age or other factor, and circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional.'
'The patient and pharmacist must both be physically present at the approved pharmacy premises, for consultation with the patient to occur prior to supply.'

The pharmacist is an 'approved pharmacist' — holds general registration under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law (NSW); is employed or engaged in an 'approved pharmacy'; has successfully completed the specified training options; and has provided NSW Health with their full name, contact details, pharmacist registration number, intended services and location of services via the expanded-services application form.

Supply occurs at an 'approved pharmacy' — offers the authorised services when an approved pharmacist is present; maintains up-to-date service availability listings via Healthdirect Australia; and has a consulting room that is not used for any other purpose, fully enclosed with adequate privacy, adequate lighting, comfortable ambient temperature, a hand sanitisation facility, ready access to a hand washing facility, and sufficient floor area for the patient, an accompanying person and the pharmacist.

exclusion.text: The patient is under 6 years of age (not an 'applicable patient': 'An 'applicable patient' means a patient 6 years of age or over.').

The medicine is not for the management of allergic and/or nonallergic rhinitis — 'The pharmacist must only supply a medicine indicate in clause 2 for the management of allergic and/or nonallergic rhinitis.'
The medicine is not an intranasal form of Fluticasone furoate or Olopatadine with mometasone, and not an eye drop form of Olopatadine 0.1% (i.e. not a substance/form listed in clause 2).

provenance.section_heading: 2) Restricted substance to which this instrument applies

exclusion.text: The quantity supplied exceeds the duration of management specified in the Practice Standard and the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack does not exceed the specified quantity (i.e. the clause 3(c) exception does not apply).
The supply quantity would result in supply for a period longer than 12 weeks (clause 3(d) prohibits this 'despite clause 3(c)').
The patient and pharmacist are not both physically present at the approved pharmacy premises, or consultation with the patient did not occur prior to supply.
The pharmacist is not an 'approved pharmacist' or the premises are not an 'approved pharmacy' (including failure to meet the consulting room requirements).

An 'age or other factor' limitation on supply set by the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Allergic and Nonallergic Rhinitis precludes supply to this patient (clause 3(e) incorporates those limitations into this instrument).

exclusion_exceptions.text: 'If the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack of the medicine exceeds the quantity specified in the Practice Standard, the pharmacist may supply the medicine in the smallest available size.' Note: clause 3(d) overrides this — supply still must not exceed 12 weeks.

diagnosis_pathways.name: Supply of a restricted substance for allergic and non-allergic rhinitis — ordered conditions (clause 3)

steps.description: Clause 3(a): 'The pharmacist must only supply a medicine indicate in clause 2 for the management of allergic and/or nonallergic rhinitis.' Confirm the presentation is allergic and/or nonallergic rhinitis and the medicine is an intranasal form of Fluticasone furoate or Olopatadine with mometasone, or an eye drop form of Olopatadine 0.1% (clause 2).

gates.criterion: Medicine is an intranasal form of Fluticasone furoate or Olopatadine with mometasone, or an eye drop form of Olopatadine 0.1% (clause 2), and is for the management of allergic and/or nonallergic rhinitis

steps.description: Clause 3(b) and 3(c): 'The pharmacist must not supply a medicine indicated in clause 2 in a quantity that exceeds the duration of management specified in the Practice Standard except in the circumstances described in clause 3(c) of this instrument.' 'If the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack of the medicine exceeds the quantity specified in the Practice Standard, the pharmacist may supply the medicine in the smallest available size.'

gates.criterion: Supply quantity does not exceed the duration of management specified in the Practice Standard (unless the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack exceeds the specified quantity)

steps.description: Clause 3(d): 'Despite clause 3(c), the pharmacist must not supply a medicine indicated in clause 2 of this instrument in a quantity which would result in supply for a period that is longer than 12 weeks.' Absolute cap on total supply period, overriding the smallest-pack exception.

gates.criterion: Total supply period is not longer than 12 weeks

steps.description: Clause 3(e): 'The pharmacist acts in accordance with the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Allergic and Nonallergic Rhinitis approved by the Chief Health Officer and published on the NSW Health website, including in relation to any limitations on the supply of medicines indicated in clause 2, to a patient based on their age or other factor, and circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional.'

gates.criterion: No age or other factor limitation precludes supply, and no referral circumstance applies under the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Allergic and Nonallergic Rhinitis

steps.description: Clause 3(f): 'The pharmacist must provide NSW Health with their full name, contact details, pharmacist registration number, intended services and location of services via the form at: https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/pharmaceutical/Pages/expanded-services-application.aspx.' (prerequisite to practising under this instrument, per the 'approved pharmacist' definition).

gates.criterion: Pharmacist has provided NSW Health with their full name, contact details, pharmacist registration number, intended services and location of services via the expanded-services application form

steps.description: Clause 3(g): 'The patient and pharmacist must both be physically present at the approved pharmacy premises, for consultation with the patient to occur prior to supply.' Consultation must occur before any supply is made. Clause 3(h): the name of the pharmacist providing the consultation as shown in the AHPRA Register of Pharmacists must be displayed at or near the consultation room.

gates.criterion: Patient and pharmacist both physically present at the approved pharmacy premises and consultation occurs prior to supply

steps.description: Definitions (clause 5): 'An 'applicable patient' means a patient 6 years of age or over.' Confirm the patient meets the minimum age for supply under this instrument.

gates.criterion: Patient is 6 years of age or over

steps.description: Clause 3(i): 'Pharmacists must make a full clinical record of the consultation using secure digital software. Records must be stored securely for a minimum of seven (7) years and must contain:' patient identification details; date of consultation; pharmacist name and Healthcare Provider Identifier - Individual; information relevant to the diagnosis or management; any clinical opinion reached; actions and management plan taken; particulars of any medication supplied (name, form, strength and quantity); notes on information or advice given; any consent given; and any referrals made.

Clause 3(j): 'The pharmacist must seek the patient's consent to share a record of the consultation and any subsequent consultations (including adverse events) with the patient's usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice, where the patient has one, following consent by the patient. If the patient consents to the disclosure, the record must be shared within a week following the consultation.'

gates.criterion: Patient consents to disclosure of the consultation record to their usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice

treatments.notes: Clause 2: 'Intranasal forms of: Fluticasone furoate'. Supply limited to the management of allergic and/or nonallergic rhinitis (clause 3(a)). Applicable patient must be 6 years of age or over. Quantity/duration governed by the 'NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Allergic and Nonallergic Rhinitis' (separate document, not part of this PDF); clause 3(c) permits supply of the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack if that pack exceeds the specified quantity, but clause 3(d) caps total supply at 12 weeks ('must not supply … in a quantity which would result in supply for a period that is longer than 12 weeks'). Strength, dose, frequency, quantity and duration are NOT printed in this instrument. No pregnancy or lactation caveat is printed in this document; no paediatric caveat beyond the 6-year minimum age is printed.

provenance.section_heading: 2) Restricted substance to which this instrument applies

treatments.notes: Clause 2: 'Intranasal forms of: Olopatadine with mometasone'. Supply limited to the management of allergic and/or nonallergic rhinitis (clause 3(a)). Quantity/duration governed by the 'NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Allergic and Nonallergic Rhinitis' (separate document, not part of this PDF); clause 3(c) smallest-pack exception applies subject to the clause 3(d) 12-week supply cap. Strength, dose, frequency, quantity and duration are NOT printed in this instrument. No pregnancy or lactation caveat is printed in this document; no paediatric caveat beyond the 6-year minimum age is printed.

Quantity/duration governed by the 'NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Allergic and Nonallergic Rhinitis' (separate document, not part of this PDF); clause 3(c) smallest-pack exception applies subject to the clause 3(d) 12-week supply cap. Dose, frequency, quantity and duration are NOT printed in this instrument. No pregnancy or lactation caveat is printed in this document; no paediatric caveat beyond the 6-year minimum age is printed.

red_flags.trigger_text: '… circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional.' (clause 3(e), as specified in the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Allergic and Nonallergic Rhinitis)
'… any limitations on the supply of medicines indicated in clause 2, to a patient based on their age or other factor …' (clause 3(e))
'An 'applicable patient' means a patient 6 years of age or over.' — a patient below 6 years of age is not eligible for supply under this instrument.
'Despite clause 3(c), the pharmacist must not supply a medicine indicated in clause 2 of this instrument in a quantity which would result in supply for a period that is longer than 12 weeks.'

routine: circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional (clause 3(e) — circumstances as specified in the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Allergic and Nonallergic Rhinitis)

review_followup.when: Within a week following the consultation, if the patient consents to the disclosure
review_followup.what: Share the record of the consultation and any subsequent consultations (including adverse events) with the patient's usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice, where the patient has one (clause 3(j)).

review_followup.when: For a minimum of seven (7) years following the consultation
review_followup.what: Store the full clinical record of the consultation securely using secure digital software (clause 3(i), page 2-3).
'This authority is cancelled on 1 March 2027, unless earlier cancelled.' (clause 7 Cancellation) — the authorisation ceases on this date.

review_followup.when: At the point where cumulative supply would result in supply for a period longer than 12 weeks
review_followup.what: 'Despite clause 3(c), the pharmacist must not supply a medicine indicated in clause 2 of this instrument in a quantity which would result in supply for a period that is longer than 12 weeks.' (clause 3(d)) — no further supply may be made beyond the 12-week cap.

conditions: 'The pharmacist must provide NSW Health with their full name, contact details, pharmacist registration number, intended services and location of services via the form at: https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/pharmaceutical/Pages/expanded-services-application.aspx.' (clause 3(f))

'The pharmacist must seek the patient's consent to share a record of the consultation and any subsequent consultations (including adverse events) with the patient's usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice, where the patient has one, following consent by the patient. If the patient consents to the disclosure, the record must be shared within a week following the consultation.' (clause 3(j))

open_questions.topic: Dose, strength (for intranasal agents), frequency, quantity and duration of management are not printed in this instrument
open_questions.observed: Clause 2 lists 'Intranasal forms of: Fluticasone furoate; Olopatadine with mometasone AND Eye drop forms of: Olopatadine 0.1%' with no dose, frequency, quantity or duration. Clause 3(b) refers to 'the duration of management specified in the Practice Standard'.
open_questions.why_unclear: The 'NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Allergic and Nonallergic Rhinitis' is a separate document not included in this PDF. Nothing was inferred; treatment dose/frequency/duration fields are left blank.

open_questions.topic: Referral circumstances and age/other factor supply limitations are deferred to a separate document
open_questions.observed: Clause 3(e) incorporates 'any limitations on the supply of medicines indicated in clause 2, to a patient based on their age or other factor, and circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional' from the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Allergic and Nonallergic Rhinitis.
open_questions.why_unclear: The specific trigger wording, thresholds, referral destinations and urgency levels are not printed in this instrument, so RF-1 and RF-2 are qualitative (structured: null) and the referral block lists only routine referral wording.

open_questions.topic: Two-column training requirements table garbled in text extraction
open_questions.observed: The 'approved pharmacist' training options render as interleaved column fragments, e.g. 'The Queensland / James Cook University's / University of / Prescribing / Extended community / Technology's Safe OR / training pharmacists course (subject / prescribing and quality / PC6300 only). / use of medicines course AND Clinical / James Cook University's / Extended community practice / pharmacists course (subjects PC6100 and PC6200 only).'
open_questions.why_unclear: Row/column alignment cannot be reconstructed reliably from flat text; INC-8 summarises the requirement as 'the specified training options' rather than transcribing the table cells, which appear to offer alternative university course pathways (Queensland University of Technology; James Cook University PC6300, PC6100, PC6200) with OR/AND connectors.

open_questions.observed: '6) Commencement — This authority commences on publication.' The instrument is 'Dated: 25 February 2026' and the instrument it revokes was 'dated 30 January 2025'.
open_questions.why_unclear: The publication date (and therefore the exact effective date) is not stated in the document; effective_date records the date of the instrument plus this note.

open_questions.topic: Clause 3(a) contains an apparent typographical error
open_questions.observed: 'The pharmacist must only supply a medicine indicate in clause 2 for the management of allergic and/or nonallergic rhinitis.' (printed as 'indicate', not 'indicated').
open_questions.why_unclear: Transcribed as printed with the note '[printed as indicate]'; meaning is unambiguous, so no reinterpretation was applied.

open_questions.topic: This instrument has no 'provide records on request to NSW Health' clause and no explicit adverse-event reporting clause
open_questions.observed: Clauses are a-k: (a) indication, (b) duration/quantity, (c) smallest pack, (d) 12-week cap, (e) Practice Standard, (f) NSW Health registration form, (g) both present, (h) name displayed, (i) clinical record, (j) consent-based sharing, (k) codes of conduct. No inspection-on-request clause and no TGA/adverse-event notification clause appears (unlike some companion authorities).
open_questions.why_unclear: notifiable.required was set to true only for the notifications the document expressly requires (NSW Health registration form and consent-based record sharing); no inspection or adverse-event reporting obligation was invented.

open_questions.observed: Clause 3(i) begins on page 2 ('Records must be stored securely for a minimum of seven (7) years and must contain:') and its bullet list continues on page 3 (consent and referrals bullets).
open_questions.why_unclear: review_followup provenance uses page 2 (where the retention period is printed); the continuation bullets are on page 3.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Obtain the current 'NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Allergic and Nonallergic Rhinitis' and transcribe its duration of management and quantity limits, age or other factor supply limitations, and referral circumstances — these govern supply under this Authority but are not printed in this PDF.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Clinical limits and referral triggers are incorporated by reference (clause 3(b), 3(e)); the prescribing module cannot evaluate eligibility or escalation without them. Note the separate absolute 12-week cap in clause 3(d) IS printed and captured.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm which approved-pharmacist training pathway local pharmacists have completed (Queensland University of Technology 'Safe prescribing and quality use of medicines course' subject PC6300, and/or James Cook University 'Extended community practice pharmacists course' subjects PC6100 and PC6200, as rendered in the garbled table).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Training requirements are a condition of being an 'approved pharmacist'; the source table is two-column and interleaved in the text extraction, so the exact OR/AND structure must be verified against the PDF.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Verify each pharmacist/pharmacy has completed the NSW Health expanded-services registration (full name, contact details, pharmacist registration number, intended services and location of services via https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/pharmaceutical/Pages/expanded-services-application.aspx) and displays the consulting pharmacist's name at or near the consultation room.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Clause 3(f) and 3(h) are conditions of supply; local go-live must confirm the registration and signage process.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the instrument is current before go-live: dated 25 February 2026, commences on publication, cancelled 1 March 2027 unless earlier cancelled, and revokes the earlier instrument dated 30 January 2025.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Jurisdictionally time-limited authority; commencement (publication) date is not printed, so currency must be checked on the NSW Health website.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm local policy for consent-based record sharing with the patient's usual treating medical practitioner within a week, including use of a secure digital messaging platform (footnote 1: 'Use of a secure digital messaging platform is considered best practice').
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Sharing mechanism, platform and local workflow are left to the pharmacy/practice.
